what_it_states: (epsilon,delta)-DP (delta>0) additive noise for T-dimensional queries with l2 sensitivity (Euclidean-ball shifts). Theorem 3.1 / B.1: as T -> infinity, for delta <= delta_star (existence; numerically tabulated lower bounds), no additive noise with the same MSE beats the Gaussian mechanism's optimal delta in the liminf sense (via Lemma 3.1 affine test, Proposition 3.1 supporting-line Jensen, Lemma 3.2 asymptotics of the Gaussian privacy function, Proposition B.1 downward closure, Lemma 3.3 Haar symmetrization over the full orthogonal group). Section 4 and Appendix C: Spherical Generalized Gamma (SGG) family, one-dimensional privacy-loss integral (Lemma 4.1), radial monotonicity (Prop 4.1), shift monotonicity (Lemma 4.2), eta-tight oracle with interval arithmetic (Lemma 4.3, Algorithms 1-3), parameterized mechanism (Algorithm 4, Theorem C.1), numerical MSE minimization over (alpha,beta,p) by binary search and Bayesian optimization (Algorithms 5-6) with reported low-dimensional MSE reductions as an existence observation, FFT composition accounting (Prop 4.2, Lemma D.1, Algorithm 7); Appendix E identifies an error in Ji-Li 2024 Theorem 5 with a numerical table.
what_it_does_not_state: No pure-DP (delta=0) fixed-dimension optimality; no l1-diamond (or any non-Euclidean) sensitivity result; the Haar step requires the sensitivity set to be invariant under the full orthogonal group, which the closed l1 diamond is not; the only finite-dimensional MSE optimization is a numerical search inside the SGG family (continuous-density spherical laws); no all-law squared-Euclidean value, selector or unique-law equality for the registered model; no staircase optimizer; no mixed-cost all-law bound E||Z||_2^2 >= (2/3) inf E||Z||_1^2; no rounded-core selector.
